preamble: Five 12s are not further defined in their clues.

indicators.note: the opening word splits into a preposition placing one piece inside another

parts.note: read as two words, 'In sure'; the second word is taken as written
tat is cheap, worthless stuff

explanation.surface: Someone insures a pile of junk, perhaps a car that is still standing.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word must be split in two, giving a placement instruction and a word to hold the junk. Tat is British slang for tasteless rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Stature means status or reputation, the standing a person holds in others' eyes.

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so the letters are formed into something new
the answer together with these letters makes the phrase, so they must be removed from it to get back

parts.note: the phrase whose letters hold the answer plus the extra word
taken as written; these are the letters removed

explanation.surface: A woman wears a stylish pork-pie hat.
explanation.walkthrough: This works backwards: the answer plus HER, rearranged, makes PORK-PIE HAT, so take HER out of those letters and rearrange the rest. Per the preamble the answer is one of the palaces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Topkapi in Istanbul was the main residence of the Ottoman sultans, so it fits the preamble's palace theme.

clue.text: Washington gallery exhibits a friendly place

indicators.note: to exhibit is to put on show, so the letters are on display inside the words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A Washington art gallery is praised as a welcoming place to visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washington gallery' looks like a museum name, but it simply holds the letters. Tonga was named the Friendly Islands by Captain Cook.
explanation.definitionFit: Cook's name for the Tongan archipelago, the Friendly Islands, makes it a cryptic description of the Pacific kingdom.

clue.text: Nice location a compiler spotted in Jordan first, perhaps

indicators.note: this sets the order, putting the larger piece before the single letter
something spotted in a place is seen inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: the Jordan is a river
the crossword compiler refers to themself as I
taken as written
surface padding: it marks Jordan as just one example of a river

explanation.surface: The setter tells of being seen in Jordan before heading to a resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective; the capital letter at the start of the clue hides that. 'perhaps' marks Jordan as one example of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice is one of the main resort cities on the French Riviera, the Mediterranean coastline of southern France.

clue.text: Fruit of wasting the end of the month attached to bed

indicators.note: wasting away loses something, here the tail letter of the word that follows
being attached means joined on, so one piece is fixed to the next

parts.note: the month is April, cluing the last letter it loses
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A fruit left to waste at the end of the month on a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the month' could be any month; only April shortened by one letter fits with a bed after it.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a soft orange stone fruit related to the peach and plum.

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
achy means aching, sore

explanation.surface: A fashionable man discovers that working out hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dandy' reads as a noun, a vain dresser, but here it is the adjective meaning excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal American use both words mean fine or excellent, as in 'everything's just dandy'.

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I
to slam is to criticise harshly; with I as subject it takes no S
taken as written
poor quality is bad

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler is attacking some dreadful city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter criticises' reads as third person, but Setter is I, so the verb becomes I SLAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Islamabad is the capital city of Pakistan, built as a planned capital in the 1960s.

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls in cricket
a run is the unit of scoring in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricket rule book produced at excessive length.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is TOO MUCH, so the definition reads 'too much production'. 'cricket terms' supplies two words from the game, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: An overrun is output or spending beyond what was planned, as in a production run that exceeds its target.

clue.text: Finds the ark built right with branches outside

indicators.note: being outside means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the rest

parts.note: boughs are the branches of a tree

indicators.note: something built is assembled from parts, so the letters are put together in a new form

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone discovers Noah's ark, properly built and with branches around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finds' looks like a verb but is a plural noun, discoveries. The ark's letters are rearranged and R added before the branches go round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakthroughs are important discoveries or sudden advances, the kind of finds that change a field.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lively and fast, as in a quick pace
second meaning: a beating with an open hand on the bottom

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read like one phrase about swift discipline, but each is a separate meaning of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for a lively, vigorous pace and a noun for smacking a child as a penalty.

indicators.note: poor results are in a bad state, so the letters are in a state of disorder

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A pupil reports disappointing exam grades to a teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: A levels are the English school-leaving exams. Per the preamble the answer is one of the palaces, with no further definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Versailles near Paris was the grand royal residence of Louis XIV, so it fits the preamble's palace theme.

clue.text: 27's house is regularly clean, kept in step

indicators.note: what is kept in something is held inside it

parts.note: a pace is a single step

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is used

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: The royal residence is cleaned on schedule while staff keep in step.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is KING, so the definition is 'king's house'. Take the even letters of 'clean' and put them inside a step.
explanation.definitionFit: A palace is the official residence of a monarch, the home of a king or queen.

indicators.note: an amendment is a change, so the letters are altered in order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

indicators.note: the first means the opening letter only of the preceding name

parts.note: the initial of the surname

explanation.surface: A history lesson on the first change to the US Constitution under President Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to the US Constitution's First Amendment; instead Abraham plus Lincoln's initial are rearranged. Per the preamble the answer is a palace.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alhambra in Granada is a Moorish fortress and royal residence, so it fits the preamble's palace theme.

clue.text: Leaving it to be dealt with properly is not his style

definitions.text: Leaving it to be dealt with properly is not his style
definitions.note: the whole clue describes the answer

indicators.note: cards that are dealt are shuffled first, so these letters get redistributed

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
completes the description: he will not leave crime to the proper authorities

explanation.surface: A man who never leaves a job to be handled by the right people.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening two words are the fodder and the whole sentence is the definition: such a person will not leave crime to the police and courts.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigilante is a self-appointed enforcer who punishes wrongdoers without legal authority instead of trusting police or courts.

indicators.note: to correct is to put right, so the letters are changed into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
key means essential, vital

explanation.surface: Picking the right option is vital in any sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correct' reads as an adjective describing the choice, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice hockey is a team game played on ice with sticks and a puck, a sport in its own right.

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the preceding word

parts.note: the closing letter of the word
bony means very thin, slim to the point of showing bone

explanation.surface: A dieter's waist is at last slender and toned.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs the surface into the next clue but the two are solved separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is a very dark wood, and the word is used as an adjective for a deep black colour.

indicators.note: skimming takes the top layer off, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: butter is a dairy fat

explanation.surface: Continuing the dieter's tale, slimness comes from taking the fat off.
explanation.walkthrough: Skimming milk takes the cream off the top; here it takes the top letter off a fat. In a down-reading sense the top is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to speak or voice words, so it is a direct synonym of the verb meaning to speak.

clue.text: Occasionally, military leaders get in touch more than necessary

indicators.note: to get in is to enter, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: leaders go in front, so the opening letters are taken

parts.note: the initial letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Army commanders sometimes keep in contact more than is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasionally' looks like an alternate-letters signal, but it is fodder; 'leaders' takes the first letters of it and the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Too much describes an excess, an amount beyond what is needed or wanted.

clue.text: Record about spots compiler has to drop fast

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc, a record
a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin
the compiler is I, and I have shortens to I've

explanation.surface: A setter with a recording of spots must suddenly plunge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compiler has' becomes I'VE, the setter speaking of themself; the apostrophe is dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash-dive is a submarine's emergency rapid descent, so as a verb it means to plunge downward quickly.

clue.text: Found in haste, a merchant ship

indicators.note: what is found in something lies within it, here inside the run of words

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A merchant ship founded in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'merchant ship' looks like one definition, but only the last word defines; the start of 'merchant' supplies the end of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamer is a ship driven by steam engines, once the standard ocean-going vessel.

clue.text: Mount with vigour outside in a state

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: vim is energy, vigour
Etna is a volcano in Sicily

explanation.surface: Someone climbs a horse or a mountain energetically, while in a flustered state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' wants to be a verb; it is a mountain, the Sicilian volcano. 'in a state' sounds like being upset, but 'a state' means a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Vietnam is a sovereign country in Southeast Asia, and a state is a nation with its own government.

clue.text: Leave half the quantity first in the body

indicators.note: this sets the order, putting the shortened word in front
half means only part is kept, so the back portion is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, losing its last four letters
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone is told to leave, with half the amount going to their body first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'body' means an organisation, not a person's frame. A quango is a British term for a public agency.
explanation.definitionFit: A quango is a quasi-autonomous non-governmental organisation, a semi-public administrative body funded by government.

clue.text: Oh no! Swinging sixties pop star appears in Hawaii

definitions.note: the place is in Hawaii, so it is defined by location

indicators.note: swinging means moving to and fro, so the letters are moved about

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
Lulu is a Scottish singer who had hits in the 1960s, including 'Shout'

explanation.surface: A fan gasps as a star from the Swinging Sixties shows up in Hawaii.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swinging sixties' looks like a fixed phrase for the 1960s, but 'Swinging' is the signal working on the exclamation before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Honolulu is the capital and largest city of the US state of Hawaii, on Oahu.

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and the seat of a bishop's see
taken as written, a second see

explanation.walkthrough: The one word stands for two sees: Ely, an English diocese, and SEE itself. Per the preamble the answer is a palace.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elysée Palace in Paris is the official residence of the French president, fitting the preamble's palace theme.

indicators.note: something lost has gone astray, so the letters wander out of order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone discovers their key has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive but is the exclamation of surprise, as in 'My! What a mess'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise or alarm, interjections blurted out at an unexpected shock.

indicators.note: soaking something up takes it inside, so one piece absorbs another

parts.note: to bum is to sponge or cadge off others

indicators.note: including means taking in, so one piece holds another

parts.note: cha is a British slang word for tea
the answer to clue 27, the second half of 10's answer

explanation.surface: A sponge cake absorbs the tea, along with a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sponge' reads as a noun but is a verb, to scrounge. Per the preamble the answer is a palace.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckingham Palace in London is the official residence of the British monarch, fitting the preamble's palace theme.

clue.text: 25 offering some resistance with limits to young and old alike

parts.note: the ohm is the unit of electrical resistance

indicators.note: limits are the edges, so only the outermost letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
the first and last letters of the word
surface padding: it shows both words are treated the same way

explanation.surface: Young and old alike offer a little resistance and cry out.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is YIKES, so the definition is another cry of alarm. 'alike' shows the same limits apply to both words.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are interjections of shock or dismay, exclamations used when something alarming happens.

indicators.note: can be suggests what something might become, so the letters may form a new word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A single person lighting up can annoy those nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a plain statement about smokers; 'can be' does the work of signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Irksome means annoying or tiresome, something that bothers or vexes people.
